pipeline_mapping: **d22's third prior-art model and its only one with a bottom-up per-mission cost anchor.** The paper proposes an explicit cost structure for interplanetary commodity exploitation: C_commodity_total = $50B annual global (USA share $25B), derived from 5% of US industrial GDP (~$2T) as 'a reasonable amount to initially allocate to cosmic industry costs' (p14); **the case study's total estimated cost for a mission to mine an asteroid = $5 billion, stated by the authors themselves as 'almost certainly low'** (p14) - order-of-magnitude context for our per-mission spend rows; residual-value chain: tellurium residuals A=$1B / B=$1T production value / C=$10B (pp14-15); shadow costs R_commodity = $100M global, allocated to the USA at $50M via eq.(39)-(40) (p15). Value-side context: space economy ~$251B in 2007 with >60% commercial (p2); a 30-m asteroid holds $25-50B of platinum, an 80-m one >$100B of materials, a 200-m metallic body ~$30B 'at today's prices', and a high-PGM 500-m body the equivalent of all PGMs ever mined on Earth (p3). No re-pin proposed: figures are 2017 order-of-magnitude estimates for model calibration, not measurements - they bracket rather than contradict our rows. Fills d22's brief bullet 'published TEAs ... with inputs mappable to ours' at the macro level.
